UPSTREAM: ACPI / platform: Pay attention to parent device's resources Given following simplified device hierarchy: // PCI device having BAR0 (RMEM) split between 4 GPIO devices. Device (P2S) { Name (_ADR, 0x000d0000) Device (GPO0) { Name (_HID, "INT3452") Name (_UID, 1) Name (_CRS, ResourceTemplate () { Memory32Fixed (ReadWrite, 0, 0x4000, RMEM + 0x0000) }) } Device (GPO1) { Name (_HID, "INT3452") Name (_UID, 2) Name (_CRS, ResourceTemplate () { Memory32Fixed (ReadWrite, 0, 0x4000, RMEM + 0x4000) }) } Device (GPO2) { Name (_HID, "INT3452") Name (_UID, 3) Name (_CRS, ResourceTemplate () { Memory32Fixed (ReadWrite, 0, 0x4000, RMEM + 0x8000) }) } Device (GPO3) { Name (_HID, "INT3452") Name (_UID, 4) Name (_CRS, ResourceTemplate () { Memory32Fixed (ReadWrite, 0, 0x4000, RMEM + 0xc000) }) } } The current ACPI platform enumeration code allocates resources from the global MMIO resource pool (/proc/iomem) for all the four GPIO devices. After this PCI core calls pcibios_resource_survey() to allocate resources for all PCI devices including the parent device for these GPIO devices (P2S). Since that resource range has already been reserved the allocation fails. The reason for this is that we never bother with parent device's resources when ACPI platform devices are created. Fix this by checking whether there is a parent device and in that case make sure we assign correct parent resource to the resources for the child ACPI platform device. Currently we only deal with parent devices if they are PCI devices but we may expand this later to cover other bus types as well. Reported-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@google.com> Signed-off-by: Mika Westerberg <mika.westerberg@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com> (cherry picked from commit a252d881c5585f5a25d4beeca23806b4fea116eb) Signed-off-by: Azhar Shaikh <azhar.shaikh@intel.com> BUG=b:35572567 TEST=On boot up do not see "address conflict" message anymore. Change-Id: I08bd0ce6ab996cc4874e75c416a2c29b0280bcf2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/431197 Commit-Ready: Azhar Shaikh <azhar.shaikh@intel.corp-partner.google.com> Tested-by: Azhar Shaikh <azhar.shaikh@intel.corp-partner.google.com> Reviewed-by: Wayne Boyer <wayne.boyer@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Benson Leung <bleung@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: config: Make PINCTRL_BROXTON as a loadable module Change PINCTRL_BROXTON from a built-in module to a loadable module. By making the module loadable, driver will be loaded after PCI core has enumerated the devices making the MMIO space available for the parent PCI device. Otherwise the driver requests the resource before the parent PCI device gets a chance to do anything. dmesg output with in-built-module: [ 0.233438] gpiochip_find_base: found new base at 434 [ 0.233484] gpiochip_add_data: registered GPIOs 434 to 511 on device: INT3452:00 [ 0.233488] GPIO chip INT3452:00: created GPIO range 0->77 ==> INT3452:00 PIN 0->77 [ 0.233864] gpiochip_find_base: found new base at 357 [ 0.233904] gpiochip_add_data: registered GPIOs 357 to 433 on device: INT3452:01 [ 0.233907] GPIO chip INT3452:01: created GPIO range 0->76 ==> INT3452:01 PIN 0->76 [ 0.234200] gpiochip_find_base: found new base at 310 [ 0.234238] gpiochip_add_data: registered GPIOs 310 to 356 on device: INT3452:02 [ 0.234241] GPIO chip INT3452:02: created GPIO range 0->46 ==> INT3452:02 PIN 0->46 [ 0.234488] gpiochip_find_base: found new base at 267 [ 0.234526] gpiochip_add_data: registered GPIOs 267 to 309 on device: INT3452:03 [ 0.234530] GPIO chip INT3452:03: created GPIO range 0->42 ==> INT3452:03 PIN 0->42 .. .. [ 0.267497] pci 0000:00:0d.0: can't claim BAR 0 [mem 0xd0000000-0xd0ffffff 64bit]: address conflict with INT3452:03 [mem 0xd0c00000-0xd0c03fff] .. .. [ 7.792994] broxton-pinctrl INT3452:00: request() failed for pin 10 [ 7.793005] broxton-pinctrl INT3452:00: pin-10 (INT3452:00:444) status -16 [ 7.793009] gpio-444 (?): gpiod_request: status -16 [ 7.793011] export_store: status -16 [ 7.812526] broxton-pinctrl INT3452:01: request() failed for pin 35 [ 7.812537] broxton-pinctrl INT3452:01: pin-35 (INT3452:01:392) status -16 [ 7.812541] gpio-392 (?): gpiod_request: status -16 [ 7.812543] export_store: status -16 dmesg output with loadble module: [ 7.230765] gpiochip_find_base: found new base at 434 [ 7.230840] gpiochip_add_data: registered GPIOs 434 to 511 on device: INT3452:00 [ 7.230844] GPIO chip INT3452:00: created GPIO range 0->77 ==> INT3452:00 PIN 0->77 [ 7.231127] gpiochip_find_base: found new base at 357 [ 7.231194] gpiochip_add_data: registered GPIOs 357 to 433 on device: INT3452:01 [ 7.231198] GPIO chip INT3452:01: created GPIO range 0->76 ==> INT3452:01 PIN 0->76 [ 7.231415] gpiochip_find_base: found new base at 310 [ 7.231487] gpiochip_add_data: registered GPIOs 310 to 356 on device: INT3452:02 [ 7.231490] GPIO chip INT3452:02: created GPIO range 0->46 ==> INT3452:02 PIN 0->46 [ 7.231658] gpiochip_find_base: found new base at 267 [ 7.231726] gpiochip_add_data: registered GPIOs 267 to 309 on device: INT3452:03 [ 7.231730] GPIO chip INT3452:03: created GPIO range 0->42 ==> INT3452:03 PIN 0->42 pin_request() function does not fail in this case. FROMLIST: fix minor error in YUV2RGB matrix used in shader The matrix used for YCbCr to RGB is listed in Wiki https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YCbCr; There is minor error in the matrix constant: 0.0625=16/256 should be 16.0/255, and 0.5=128.0/256 should be 128.0/255. Note that conversion from a 0-255 byte number to 0-1.0 float is to divide by 255 instead of 256. That's we get 255=1.0f. By the constant change we can see the CSC result is bit aligned with Wiki conversion result and FFMPeg result. Otherwise in some situation, there will be one bit difference Bugzilla: https://bugs.freedesktop.org/show_bug.cgi?id=100854 Signed-off-by: Kristian H.
